name: Recruit Training Command, Great Lakes
explanation: Enlisted boot camp for the Navy, at Naval Station Great Lakes, Illinois. Recruit training was 10 weeks in September 1997.
civilian: This is where a new sailor learns to live in the Navy before going on to a technical school.

name: USS Tortuga (LSD-46)
explanation: A Whidbey Island-class dock landing ship. It carries Marines with their vehicles and landing craft, and launches the craft from a well deck that floods. Assault Craft Unit 4 (ACU 4) was the craft unit on this TAD. The dates of this assignment have not been entered.
civilian: A ship that carries Marines and their boats and vehicles to a beach. ACU 4 ran the landing craft.

name: Naval Training Center Great Lakes
explanation: The Navy's training center at Great Lakes, Illinois. The emblem shown is the seal of Naval Station Great Lakes, the installation's current name. The dates of this assignment have not been entered.
open: NTC Great Lakes: dates not entered.
civilian: The Navy's big training base north of Chicago.

name: Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station San Diego
explanation: A shore command that ran Navy computer and telecommunications services in San Diego. The shadowbox lists the NEC for this tour as 1589, calibration.
civilian: A land-based communications station, not a ship.

name: USS Frank Cable (AS-40)
explanation: A submarine tender: a ship that repairs, supplies, and houses the crews of submarines. In these years her home port was Guam. The NEC on the shadowbox for this tour is 1589. The three Navy E awards dated 2001, 2002, and 2003 fall in this tour.
civilian: A repair ship for submarines, not a submarine itself.

name: EOD Mobile Unit Five
explanation: Explosive Ordnance Disposal Mobile Unit Five, a Navy bomb-disposal unit then based in Guam. Assignment to the unit is not the same as being a bomb-disposal technician. The shadowbox lists the NEC as 9613, a communications specialty. The Royal Thai Navy hosted Cobra Gold twice. An Australian Clearance Diving Team was the partner on Talisman Saber twice.
civilian: The command's job was disposing of explosives. His recorded specialty there was communications.

name: Combined Joint Task Force Troy
explanation: A joint and coalition task force in Iraq in 2006, during Operation Iraqi Freedom, stood up against roadside bombs. EOD Mobile Unit 11 was the partner. The 52nd Ordnance Group and the 16th Engineer Brigade were sponsors. The Iraq campaign phase named for this tour is National Resolution.
civilian: A temporary headquarters in Iraq, drawn from more than one country and more than one branch.

name: 52nd Ordnance Group (EOD)
explanation: A U.S. Army explosive ordnance disposal group. Sponsor of the CJTF Troy deployment. The dates have not been entered.

name: 16th Engineer Brigade
explanation: A U.S. Army engineer brigade. Sponsor of the CJTF Troy deployment. The dates have not been entered.

name: 3rd Special Forces Group (Airborne)
explanation: A U.S. Army Special Forces group. Partner on the first CJSOTF-A deployment. The dates have not been entered.
open: 3rd Special Forces Group: dates not entered.

name: 75th Ranger Regiment
explanation: The U.S. Army's Ranger regiment. Partner on the second CJSOTF-A deployment. The dates have not been entered.

name: Southeast Regional Calibration Center
explanation: The Navy's Southeast Regional Calibration Center, at Naval Air Station Jacksonville. A calibration center checks the test equipment other commands use. The NEC on this tour is 1589, which matches that work.
civilian: A laboratory that keeps measuring tools honest.

name: Task Force Iron Shield
explanation: The individual-augmentee deployment to Iraq, about seven months, after SERCC. The 11th Air Defense Artillery Brigade was the sponsor. The campaign phase named for this tour is Iraq Sovereignty. No Task Force Iron Shield crest is on file.
civilian: He was still a sailor, working inside an Army deployment.

name: Joint Communications Support Element
explanation: A joint unit, based at MacDill Air Force Base in Florida, that sends small communications teams out quickly for special operations and other joint commanders. Reported in 2009 and detached in 2014. The NEC listed for the tour is 9613. It included the two Afghanistan deployments.
civilian: A communications unit made of every branch, not a Navy ship.

name: Combined Joint Special Operations Task Force — Afghanistan
explanation: Two Afghanistan deployments under CJSOTF-A while assigned to JCSE. The first, 2010–2011, was with 3rd Special Forces Group. The second, 2012–2013, was with the 75th Ranger Regiment. The role in the record is communications, not service as a special operator. Each tour was about seven months.
civilian: The headquarters he supported. Being the communicator for that headquarters is not the same job as the operators it commanded.

name: Naval Hospital Jacksonville
explanation: The Navy hospital at Jacksonville, Florida, and the last active-duty command. He reported in 2014 after detaching from JCSE. Last duty assignment was Naval Hospital Jacksonville, with separation processing at the personnel support detachment on Naval Air Station Jacksonville.
civilian: A hospital, not a ship. An electronics technician there maintains medical and other electronic equipment. The day-to-day job is not further described.
